title: Lists and Tables
description: Represent structured content and 2D data: choose between unordered (<ul>) and ordered (<ol>) lists, construct robust data tables (<table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tr>, <th>, <td>), and avoid layout anti-patterns.

objectives.statement: Construct correctly nested ordered (ol) and unordered (ul) list structures containing li elements.
Build accessible 2D data tables using table, thead, tbody, tr, th, and td elements.

content.title: Structuring Collections and Grids of Data
content.hook: When content is a collection of items or a 2D matrix of values, HTML provides dedicated list and table structures that communicate relationships to both users and assistive technology.
content.context: Lists group related items sequentially (`<ol>`) or non-sequentially (`<ul>`). Tables present multi-dimensional data with explicit column/row headers (`<th>`) and data cells (`<td>`).
goals: Choose between `<ol>` and `<ul>` based on whether sequence matters.
Construct properly structured data tables with `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>`.
Understand why tables are strictly for data, never for general page layouts.

content.title: List and Table Hierarchy
content.description: Lists: <ul> or <ol> -> <li> items only. Tables: <table> -> <thead> (<tr> -> <th>) + <tbody> (<tr> -> <td>). Cells must always be nested inside <tr> rows.

content.prompt: Order the nesting hierarchy of an accessible HTML table from outermost root container to innermost header cell:

feedback.correct: Spot on! `<table>` wraps `<thead>`, which contains `<tr>` rows, which contain `<th>` cells.
feedback.incorrect: Review table hierarchy: `<table>` contains section wrappers (`<thead>`/`<tbody>`), which contain rows (`<tr>`), which contain cells (`<th>`/`<td>`).

content.title: Build a Product Comparison Table
content.prompt: Construct a data table with a `<thead>` containing column headers for 'Plan' and 'Price', and a `<tbody>` with two rows for 'Basic ($10/mo)' and 'Pro ($25/mo)'.
content.starterCode: Subscription Plans

testCases.description: Table must have <thead> with <th> headers for Plan and Price
Table must have <tbody> containing at least 2 <tr> rows with <td> data cells

feedback.correct: Fantastic work! You built a semantically sound, accessible data table with headers and data rows.
feedback.incorrect: Make sure your table structure strictly follows `<table> <thead> <tr> <th>...` and `<tbody> <tr> <td>...`.

content.prompt: In early web development (1990s), developers used `<table>` tags to position navbars, sidebars, and grid layouts. Why is using tables for page layout a major anti-pattern today?

feedback.correct: Spot on! Using tables for layout destroys screen reader navigation by announcing tabular coordinates, impairs responsiveness, and pollutes HTML semantics. Modern layouts belong in CSS (Grid & Flexbox).
feedback.incorrect: Focus on the accessibility harms and maintenance problems of using data tables for visual layout.

content.title: Key Takeaways: Lists and Tables
takeaways: Use `<ul>` when order does not matter; use `<ol>` when the sequential order is meaningful.
List containers can ONLY contain `<li>` elements as direct children.
Use `<table>` strictly for two-dimensional tabular data with `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>`.
Never use `<table>` for visual layout; use modern CSS Flexbox and Grid instead.
